# Old Weirde's Incunabulum

*Page PDF 4*

THE CORSAIRS OF CAPTAIN FL ARIEL 

## Old Weirde’s Incunabulum

On occasion, I venture a little further from my hearth to enjoy a libation at the Frisky Seagoat, an inn by the naval docks in Flottenliegeplatz. What the patrons lack in decorum and intact limbs, they more than make up with tattoos depicting sea serpents and great krakens, and tall tales from the sea. 

Nevertheless, I have gathered fragments of information from Abbot Bruggeman of Manannsheim, my dear friend Professor Kikkert of Baron Henryk’s College in Marienburg, and Grandmaster Hrofil Halfdan of the Sons of Manann. Consistent accounts from the northern coasts speak of black-clad reavers dressed in reptilian cloaks, who descend on isolated coastal settlements to murder and enslave the residents. By the time local rulers muster a response, the Dark Elves are long gone — one notorious example is the ill-fated village of Debnietz, where the inhabitants were flayed and nailed to the cliffs. 

During a recent visit, I heard a yarn from a one-armed Nordlander, a gentleman of morose disposition and powerful odor. As the rain lashed on the panes, he told of a galley in full sail that blew into the Kriedeklippe Bight, two days before Mitterfruhl. She was listing badly and no crewman answered the warning cries to stay away from the rocks. When the inevitable happened and she crashed onto a reef, the salvage crew found a harrowing mystery. Bloodstains spattered the deck and other than the captain, no soul was on board. The poor wretch clung to life, pinned to the mast with barbed quarrels, his flesh horribly lacerated and his mind completely gone. 

When researching any matter related to the Elves, I find Algnar’s A Man Amongst the Elves informative. He mentions an ancient schism between the Elven folk, when those from the northern reaches of their fabled isle embraced the dark powers and rebelled against the rightful king. They were banished, or retreated, to the icy lands north of Lustria. There is little more in the Human writings I have to hand… as ever, I come up against the limits of prior scholarship. I determined to ask an Asur acquaintance for further enlightenment. 

The first mate of a Wasteland merchantman sucked on his pipe and nodded through the smoke. He had seen similar and worse. It was the Elf folk — not the haughty Elves we know in Altdorf and Marienburg, nor their cousins the ‘Wood Elves’ who dwell in the Laurelorn and Athel Loren. The Wastelander whispered of their vicious kin, the ‘Dark Elves’, who raid our coasts and attack ships from their sleek black vessels. 

One foggy evening in Erntezeit, I set out to consult with Loremaster Illissia Waysworn of the Sapherian Embassy over a delicious repast in the New World Dinery.
